data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumption is permissible if and only if the resumption protocol can reconstruct the causal fingerprint from the committed log alone without reference to the partial fragment, because the partial fragment is causally inert; resumption must be refused when the partial fragment has leaked causal state into a side channel that the resumed stream would read.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The reasoning envelope has no side channels\u2014all causal state is captured in the committed event log, making the partial fragment truly inert.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The side channel is write-only from the reasoning process's perspective and never read on resumption, making leaked state causally inert.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The side channel is checkpointed atomically with each committed event, so its state always corresponds to the last committed event regardless of truncation.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The causal fingerprint is a function of the committed event sequence. A partial fragment, being a non-event, does not enter the fingerprint. Therefore resumption is safe whenever the resumed stream's observable output depends solely on committed events. However, if the reasoning envelope writes intermediate state to a side channel (e.g., a scratchpad, cache, or environment variable) that the resumed stream reads, then the partial fragment's side-channel residue is causally potent\u2014it influences the resumed computation even though it was never a committed event. This creates a divergence between the resumed stream's fingerprint and an uninterrupted run's fingerprint. Resumption must be refused until the side channel is reconciled to the state corresponding to the last committed event.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
